stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Distant light rays enter the relaxed eye — parallel to the optical axis. Drag $F'$ along the axis to move the focal point. When the orange focus dot lands on the retina, the eye sees sharply.
stages.concept: A converging lens brings parallel rays to a point at its rear focal point $F'$. For a normal relaxed eye ($d' = 17$ mm), $F'$ sits exactly on the retina, so distant objects focus sharply on it.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: For each object distance $d$, adjust the eye's accommodation so the image lands on the retina. Press Fire (or Space) to confirm. Three targets, five shots.
stages.concept: Thin-lens conjugation: $1/f' = 1/d + 1/d'$ (unsigned distances). As $d$ decreases (object closer), $f'$ must decrease — the ciliary muscle contracts to make the crystalline more convex.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The eye has a defect: its length $d'$ is not the normal $17$ mm. Rays are hidden. Read $d$ and $d'$ from the scene labels, compute the required $f'$ on paper, drag $F'$ to that value, then Fire — one shot per target.
stages.concept: For an eye of length $d'$ to see an object at distance $d$ sharply: $f' = \dfrac{d \cdot d'}{d + d'}$. Short $d'$ (hypermétropie) needs a smaller $f'$; long $d'$ (myopie) needs a larger $f'$.

labels.tip2: set F' for each object, then fire
labels.tip3: compute f' from d and d', set F', fire

1.1: Drag the orange F' dot horizontally along the dashed optical axis to move the focal point.
1.2: The refracted rays cross at F'. When that crossing lands on the retina (the orange curve), the eye sees the distant object sharply.
1.3: For a relaxed normal eye looking at infinity, F' sits exactly on the retina — 17 mm behind the lens.

2.1: Each object distance requires a different accommodation. Closer objects need a shorter f'.
2.2: Use the thin-lens formula 1/f' = 1/d + 1/d'. For the normal eye, d' = 17 mm.
2.3: For d = 1 m (1000 mm) and d' = 17 mm: 1/f' = 1/1000 + 1/17 ≈ 0.0598, so f' ≈ 16.72 mm. Same method for the other targets.

3.1: Read the labeled coordinates on the scene: d (object distance) and d' (retina, next to the eye body).
3.2: Apply 1/f' = 1/d + 1/d'. Convert all distances to millimeters. Solve for f' before touching F'.
3.3: For an object at infinity (1/d = 0): f' = d'. For a finite d: f' = d·d' / (d + d'). Use Peek to confirm your F' value matches the sim.
